question: to the Commission Mihai Tudose (S&D) Subject:

A recent European Court of Auditors report has found that the post-COVID home renovation works funded by the Recovery and Resilience Facility have delivered lower-than-expected energy savings. According to the audit, the funds involved were primarily allocated to projects that were easy to complete, rather than to endeavours that would have significantly improved energy ratings and resulted in major energy savings. Speed was prioritised over a strategic, long-term approach. As a result, not enough attention was paid to ensuring that these projects were cost-effective. In the light of the above, is the Commission considering prioritising major renovations that can result in substantial energy savings, and does it intend to take into account the Court of Auditors’ findings concerning the need to use specific criteria to rank projects according to their expected impact on energy consumption?
